skill.name: git-operation
skill.description: Guide for writing consistent Git commit messages and running project checks before committing code changes.
skill.summary: Prepare clear Git commits with message structure, formatting, and test guidance.
skill.author: 5t111111

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline command examples, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. The skill is prompt-only and contains no prompt injection, data exfiltration, or hidden automation.

static_findings.snippet: - Always run `mise run fmt` to format the code before committing
- Always run `mise run test` before committing code changes to ensure no tests

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 18 uses Markdown inline code to name a local format check, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. The command is visible guidance for commit preparation and is not dynamically constructed.
Line 19 uses Markdown inline code to name a local test check, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. The command is visible guidance for commit preparation and is not hidden automation.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent commits and checks before code lands. This skill guides commit message structure, formatting, and test steps for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Guides English Git commit messages with concise first lines.
Explains when to add a blank line and bullet details.
Instructs agents to run mise format checks before committing.
Instructs agents to run mise test checks before committing code changes.
Focuses on commit preparation, not full Git workflow automation.
limitations: Does not define branch creation, merge, rebase, or release workflows.
Assumes the repository supports mise tasks named fmt and test.
Does not run Git commands by itself; the host agent executes requested steps.
Does not explain project-specific commit scopes or issue references.

use_cases.title: Prepare Consistent Commits
use_cases.description: Use the skill to write English commit summaries and verify formatting before committing.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Commit Quality
use_cases.description: Apply shared commit message structure and pre-commit checks across assistant-supported changes.

use_cases.title: Review Agent Changes Before Commit
use_cases.description: Ask an AI assistant to summarize edits, run checks, and produce a clear commit message.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Commit Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an English Git commit message for the current changes. Use a concise first line and add bullet details only if needed.

prompt_templates.title: Run Pre-Commit Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current changes, run the configured format and test checks, then suggest a commit message.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Staged Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the staged changes, explain the user-facing impact, and draft a commit message with a short subject and optional bullets.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Clean Commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze staged and unstaged changes separately, identify unrelated work, recommend a clean commit plan, run checks, and draft final messages.

output_examples.input: I changed button spacing and fixed a validation message.
output_examples.output: Subject: Improve button spacing and validation copy. Details mention layout polish and clearer form feedback.

output_examples.input: The assistant prepared a commit after a small refactor.
output_examples.output: It reports that formatting passed, tests passed, and the commit message is ready in English.

output_examples.input: Several unrelated files changed during one work session.
output_examples.output: It recommends separating documentation edits from source changes before committing.

best_practices: Stage only related changes before asking for a commit message.
Run the project format and test tasks before creating the commit.
Keep the first commit line short and written in English.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated changes in one commit.
Do not skip checks when source files changed.
Do not use long paragraphs in the commit subject.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It tells the host agent which checks to run when preparing a commit.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through prompt instructions.

faq.question: Does it require mise?
faq.answer: The guidance assumes mise tasks are available. Projects without those tasks need equivalent local commands.

faq.question: Can it create branches?
faq.answer: No. The skill focuses on commit preparation and message guidance.

faq.question: Can it write non-English messages?
faq.answer: The skill requires English commit messages.

faq.question: Is it safe for private repositories?
faq.answer: It does not request network access or secrets. Review any local checks before running them.
